A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CST-MLP research. All 28 pages of v1 and 41 pages of v3, including supplementary Sections S1–S6, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original lightbox and in-the-wild experiments, LSMI and NUS evaluations, and supplementary simulation, LUT, and ablation results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results using estimated white points, expanded perturbation tests, and further root-polynomial comparisons.

M1.justification: The MLP architecture, cosine loss, noise augmentation, chromaticity conversion, and multi-illuminant blending procedure are retained. Polynomial/root-polynomial outputs and LUT conversion already appeared in v1 Sections S1.2–S1.3; their greater prominence and wider evaluation in v3 do not establish a changed core method.

E1.justification: The datasets, cameras, and color-correction tasks are retained. V3 adds an in-the-wild test scenario using CCMNet-estimated white points rather than ground-truth inputs or controlled synthetic offsets (Table S2). The increased image count within the existing in-the-wild coverage belongs to E3.

E2.justification: The external baseline families remain Oracle, 2-CST, 3-CST, NN, CCCNN, and EXPINV where applicable. V3 expands corresponding comparisons with CST-MLP root-polynomial variants, including new 1D RP controls in Tables 1, 3–4, S6–S8. V1's polynomial comparison was confined to its supplementary mapping ablation.

E3.justification: Section S2.2 changes the reported in-the-wild sample size from 64 to 150 images per camera. New protocols use CCMNet without camera-specific fine-tuning and extend controlled white-point offsets from 0–3° to include 10°. The principal lightbox splits, training budget, optimizer, and error metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds robustness evidence with actual estimated white points (Table S2), a severe 10° perturbation condition (Table 3), and an unaugmented root-polynomial configuration (Table 2). These extend existing sensitivity and mapping analyses; polynomial ablations and controlled white-point perturbations were already present in v1.

E5.justification: V3 Table S2 introduces a trimmed mean excluding the largest 10% of errors, supplementing ordinary means and percentiles. This changes statistical aggregation, but neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands RP and estimated-white-point results and revises existing scores. Table 1 changes the linear 2D CST-MLP Sony mean angular error from 2.58° to 2.66°. The Pixel in-the-wild result changes from 4.47° to 3.32° alongside the larger evaluation set, so this is not a same-setting gain. V3 Table 4 corrects duplicated multi-illuminant entries using values already in v1 Table S8. Architecture-ablation ΔE results and numerous 75th-percentile entries are removed.

T1.justification: The cosine-loss formulation, linear RAW synthesis derivation, multi-illuminant blending equations, and CCT estimation algorithm retain their mathematical substance. Equation renumbering and notation adjustments do not introduce new theory, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: replacing 1D CCT with 2D chromaticity, lightweight CST prediction, approximately 22% average error reduction, compatibility with traditional illuminants, and support for mixed illumination and efficient deployment.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the unfine-tuned CCMNet experiment as a worst-case estimation scenario and discusses failure under inaccurate white points. It removes DNG-conversion dependence from the concluding limitations and drops v1's detailed polynomial-overfitting explanation. The metamerism limitation remains.

D1.justification: V3 Section 3.2 newly reports an average 250 μs DNG conversion time on an iPhone 16. V1's project-page link is omitted. Existing optimizer, training-budget, capture, preprocessing, LUT, and TinyCUDA implementation information is largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 removes Hong, Luo and Rhodes (2001), cited in v1 for polynomial camera characterization. The remaining literature and principal research positioning are substantially unchanged after matching renumbered references. CCMNet was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained. V3 integrates polynomial and white-point sensitivity discussion into the main evaluation, reorders evaluation paragraphs, revises captions and terminology, and moves references after the supplementary qualitative figures.

P2.justification: V3 comprehensively reformats the document from two columns to one, rearranges Figure 2, adds an annotated training-versus-test chromaticity plot, and restructures the ablation and LSMI tables. Tables gain RP rows and lose percentile columns, while numerous figures and tables move. The main qualitative examples and supplementary Figures S4–S12 are retained.

improvement.justification: Testing CCMNet-estimated white points strengthens practical validation beyond v1's controlled offsets, and v3 corrects the main LSMI table's duplicated multi-illuminant results. Wider RP evaluation also exposes accuracy tradeoffs. These gains are tempered by unresolved reporting inconsistencies: v3 Table 2 reports 3.32° for augmented 2D linear CST-MLP on Pixel in-the-wild data, while Table S3 retains 4.47° without explaining different evaluation subsets. The additional evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
